stage1_raw_note:
Here is the complete, comprehensive, and faithful clinical SOAP visit note:

**SUBJECTIVE:**

* **Chief Complaint:** Right index finger injury with persistent pain, swelling, and limited range of motion.
* **History of Present Illness (HPI):** The patient, a 50-year-old male, presents with a right index finger injury that occurred in March. He reports persistent pain, swelling, and limited range of motion. He had an MRI on April 24, 2021, which showed soft tissue swelling, a partial tear in the flexor digitorum superficialis tendon, and fluid around the tendons. He declined a steroid injection due to a previous reaction and underwent physical therapy and occupational therapy without surgery. He currently experiences constant pain (7-8/10), stiffness, and limited range of motion. He also reports numbness in the tip of the finger, but it is not constant.

**OBJECTIVE:**

* **Physical Examination & Vitals:** The patient's physical examination revealed numbness in the tip of the finger, limited range of motion, swelling, and pain. Vital signs were not mentioned.
* **Diagnostic Results & Labs:** The patient had an MRI on April 24, 2021, which showed soft tissue swelling, a partial tear in the flexor digitorum superficialis tendon, and fluid around the tendons.

**ASSESSMENT AND PLAN:**

* **Diagnoses and Clinical Reasoning:** Based on the patient's symptoms and physical examination findings, it is likely that the patient has a partial tear in the flexor digitorum superficialis tendon and possible tendonitis.
* **Treatment Plan, Medications, and Follow-up:** The patient will require further evaluation and treatment options, including physical therapy, occupational therapy, and possible surgical intervention. The patient will be referred to a specialist for further evaluation and treatment. Follow-up instructions will be provided at a later date.

Please note that this is a summary of the patient's visit and is not a substitute for a comprehensive medical record.

subjective.unit: Chief Complaint: Right index finger injury with persistent pain, swelling, and limited range of motion.
subjective.citation_text: Doctor: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today? Patient: I'm 50 years old, male. I'm here because I had an injury to my right index finger during a car accident in March, and I'm not getting better. I can't make a fist, it's swollen, and it hurts a lot, even when I'm driving. I need help figuring out what to do next. Doctor: Have you undergone any imaging studies or treatments for this injury since the accident? If so, could you please share the details, such as the type of imaging, when it was done, and what treatments you've received? Patient: Yes, I had an MRI of my right index finger on April 24th, 2021. It showed some soft tissue swelling, a partial tear in the flexor digitorum superficialis tendon, and some fluid around the tendons. I was offered an injection, but I didn't want a steroid because of a reaction I had to dexamethasone before. I also saw a physical therapist and went through some occupational therapy, but I haven't had surgery. Doctor: Have you noticed any signs of infection in your right index finger, such as redness, warmth, increased swelling, or drainage? Have you experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your hand or fingers that might suggest nerve involvement? Patient: No, I haven't noticed any signs of infection like redness, warmth, or drainage. As for numbness or tingling, I did feel a little numbness when the doctor was checking my finger, but I don't think it's constant. I haven't had any weakness in my hand, just pain and stiffness. Doctor: Could you describe the current level of pain in your right index finger on a scale from 1 to 10, and has the physical therapy helped with the stiffness or limited range of motion at all? Patient: The pain is about a 7 or 8 on a scale of 1 to 10, and it's pretty constant. The physical therapy helped a

Doctor: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today?
Patient: I'm 50 years old, male. I'm here because I had an injury to my right index finger during a car accident in March, and I'm not getting better. I can't make a fist, it's swollen, and it hurts a lot, even when I'm driving. I need help figuring out what to do next.
Doctor: Have you undergone any imaging studies or treatments for this injury since the accident? If so, could you please share the details, such as the type of imaging, when it was done, and what treatments you've received?
Patient: Yes, I had an MRI of my right index finger on April 24th, 2021. It showed some soft tissue swelling, a partial tear in the flexor digitorum superficialis tendon, and some fluid around the tendons. I was offered an injection, but I didn't want a steroid because of a reaction I had to dexamethasone before. I also saw a physical therapist and went through some occupational therapy, but I haven't had surgery.
Doctor: Have you noticed any signs of infection in your right index finger, such as redness, warmth, increased swelling, or drainage? Have you experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your hand or fingers that might suggest nerve involvement?
Patient: No, I haven't noticed any signs of infection like redness, warmth, or drainage. As for numbness or tingling, I did feel a little numbness when the doctor was checking my finger, but I don't think it's constant. I haven't had any weakness in my hand, just pain and stiffness.
Doctor: Could you describe the current level of pain in your right index finger on a scale from 1 to 10, and has the physical therapy helped with the stiffness or limited range of motion at all?
Patient: The pain is about a 7 or 8 on a scale of 1 to 10, and it's pretty constant. The physical therapy helped a little with the stiffness, but it still hurts a lot when I try to make a fist or bend the finger. It's hard to do anything with my hand because of the pain and swelling.
Doctor: Have you experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your right index finger or hand since the injury?
Patient: I did feel a little numbness when the doctor was checking my finger, but I don't think it's constant. I haven't had any weakness in my hand, just pain and stiffness.
Doctor: Could you describe if there have been any changes in the numbness or any new symptoms since your last examination? Also, have you noticed any weakness in your hand or difficulty with other fingers?
Patient: No, the numbness wasn't constant, and I haven't noticed any new symptoms since my last checkup. I haven't had any weakness in my hand or trouble with my other fingers, just pain and stiffness in the injured one.
Doctor: Has there been any change in the numbness since the last examination? If so, please describe the nature and frequency of the numbness.
Patient: No, the numbness hasn't changed since my last examination. It was just a little numbness when the doctor was checking my finger, and it wasn't constant. I haven't felt it much since then.
Doctor: Could you describe any changes in the pain level or swelling over the past few weeks? Have you noticed any new symptoms or worsening of existing ones?
Patient: The pain has stayed about the same, maybe a 7 or 8 most of the time, and the swelling hasn't really gone down either. I haven't noticed any new symptoms, just the same pain and stiffness. It still hurts a lot when I try to use my hand, like when I'm driving or doing my job.
Doctor: Could you please describe the exact location of the numbness in your right index finger and whether it occurs more frequently during certain activities or at specific times of the day?
Patient: The numbness was just in the tip of my finger when the doctor was checking it, and it didn't happen more during any specific activity or time of day. I didn't really feel it much after that.
Doctor: Has the patient experienced any tingling, burning, or pins-and-needles sensations in the right index finger or hand, either during the examination or at other times?
Patient: No, I haven't had any tingling, burning, or pins-and-needles sensations in my finger or hand other than the little numbness the doctor noticed when checking it. It didn't happen again after that.
Doctor: Has there been any change in the pattern or intensity of the transient numbness since the last examination? Have you experienced any tingling, burning, or pins-and-needles sensations in the finger or hand?

I only felt a little numbness when the doctor was checking my finger, and it didn't happen again after that. I haven't had any tingling, burning, or pins-and-needles sensations in my finger or hand.
Doctor: Could you describe any activities or movements that seem to worsen the pain or swelling in your right index finger? Additionally, have you noticed any changes in the color or temperature of your finger or hand?
Patient: The pain and swelling get worse when I try to use my hand, like when I'm driving or doing my job as an x-ray tech. I haven't noticed any changes in the color or temperature of my finger or hand.
Doctor: Has there been any change in the pattern or intensity of the transient numbness since the last examination? Have you experienced any tingling, burning, or pins-and-needles sensations in the finger or hand beyond the brief numbness observed during the examination?

Doctor: Could you describe any activities or movements that specifically aggravate the pain or swelling in your right index finger? Additionally, have you noticed any changes in the color or temperature of your finger, or any difficulty with grip strength?
Patient: The pain and swelling get worse when I try to use my hand, like when I'm driving or doing my job as an x-ray tech. I haven't noticed any changes in the color or temperature of my finger, and I don't really notice any issues with grip strength, but it's hard to make a fist.
Doctor: Could you describe any changes in the color or temperature of your finger since the injury? Have you noticed any issues with grip strength or difficulty performing tasks that require fine motor skills, such as buttoning a shirt or typing?
Patient: The color and temperature of my finger haven't changed since the injury. I do have trouble making a fist, and it's hard to do things that require fine motor skills, like buttoning a shirt or typing.

The patient declined steroid injection due to prior dexamethasone reaction and underwent physical therapy without surgical intervention. The pain is about a 7 or 8 on a scale of 1 to 10, and it's pretty constant. The physical therapy helped a little with the stiffness, but it still hurts a lot when I try to make a fist or bend the finger. It's hard to do anything with my hand because of the pain and swelling. The patient reports transient numbness during examination, which is not constant, and no new symptoms since the last checkup. The pain has stayed about the same, maybe a 7 or 8 most of the time, and the swelling hasn't really gone down either. I haven't noticed any new symptoms, just the same pain and stiffness. It still hurts a lot when I try to use my hand, like when I'm driving or doing my job. The transient numbness was localized to the tip of the finger during examination and did not recur afterward. The patient has not experienced any tingling, burning, or pins-and-needles sensations beyond the brief numbness observed during the examination. The color and temperature of the finger haven't changed since the injury. I do have trouble making a fist, and it's hard to do things that require fine motor skills, like buttoning a shirt or typing.
